proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 8 (identification with the trace). No errata apply.

Notation: E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, p := P.starProjection (the orthogonal projection of E onto P). All compositions are linear maps, and trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ E.

1. Idempotence. p ∘ p = p (Submodule.isIdempotentElem_starProjection: p·p = p, so p(p v) = p v for every v ∈ E). Hence L ∘ p = L ∘ (p ∘ p) = (L ∘ p) ∘ p as linear maps.

2. Cyclicity of the trace. For linear maps f, g : E → E, trace(g ∘ f) = trace(f ∘ g) (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'). With f := p and g := L ∘ p, step 1 gives trace(L ∘ p) = trace((L ∘ p) ∘ p) = trace(p ∘ (L ∘ p)).

3. Trace in an orthonormal basis. (e_k)_{k ∈ Fin N} is an orthonormal basis of E: EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose k-th vector is EuclideanSpace.single k 1. For every linear T : E → E, trace T = Σ_k ⟨e_k, T e_k⟩ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner). With T := p ∘ (L ∘ p) this gives trace(p ∘ (L ∘ p)) = Σ_k ⟨e_k, p(L(p e_k))⟩.

4. Self-adjointness. p is self-adjoint: ⟨p u, w⟩ = ⟨u, p w⟩ for all u, w ∈ E (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right). With u := e_k and w := L(p e_k), ⟨e_k, p(L(p e_k))⟩ = ⟨p e_k, L(p e_k)⟩. By symmetry of the real inner product this equals ⟨L(p e_k), p e_k⟩.

5. Combining steps 2–4, trace(L ∘ p) = Σ_{k ∈ Fin N} ⟨L(p e_k), p e_k⟩, which is the claim. For N = 0 both sides are 0. ∎

Formalization note: LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner requires `import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Trace` in the implementation file.
